name: Venus Viva
lead: Venus Viva is a nanofractional radiofrequency device marketed for skin resurfacing, including acne scars and wrinkles. Fractional RF delivers thermal energy through multiple micro-pins in a targeted pattern, which is described as shortening recovery compared with surgery or full ablation [2].

Evidence consists of small studies, including a 20-patient study of nanofractional RF for acne scars in Indian skin (Fitzpatrick types IV-V) [1] and a retrospective patient-satisfaction study [2], plus a number of small registered trials of fractional RF.
infobox: Described as shorter than ablative techniques[2]

paras: Fractional RF applies energy through arrays of micro-pins rather than across the whole skin surface, which a 2015 article says avoids surgery or full ablation and hastens recovery [2].

The 2017 Indian-skin study enrolled 20 patients aged 16-60 who received one to three treatments; its authors described acne scarring as hard to treat in darker skin and nanofractional RF as shown to be effective for cosmetic improvement of acne scars [1]. A retrospective study examined patient satisfaction after a trial of nano-fractional RF [2]. Both are small and uncontrolled.

Published studies include a 20-patient acne-scar study [1] and a retrospective satisfaction study [2]. ClinicalTrials.gov lists small completed registrations of fractional RF for acne scars (n=10 to 25) [3][4], wrinkles [5], stretch marks [6] and arm tightening [7]; registry titles do not all name a specific device, and results are not summarised here.

card.summary: Nanofractional RF resurfacing device used for acne scars and wrinkles, supported by small uncontrolled studies.
card.note: Studies are small; fractional RF has downtime and burn/pigment risks.

quick.overview:
Venus Viva is a clinic device that delivers radiofrequency energy through tiny pins to resurface skin. It is used for acne scars, wrinkles and texture.

Published work is mainly small studies, including a 20-patient acne-scar study in darker skin types.
quick.mechanism: Fractional RF heats microscopic zones of skin through micro-pins, leaving surrounding tissue intact, which is described as shortening recovery.
quick.risks: Fractional resurfacing generally causes redness and swelling; burns and pigment change are reported RF risks. Sources reviewed provide little device-specific safety data.
